source.title: Efficient Augmentation for Imbalanced Deep Learning
source.authors: Damien Dablain; C. Bellinger; B. Krawczyk; N. Chawla

record.tranche_reason: The study measures a feature-embedding train/test gap and relates it to classification outcomes, using a different gap measure from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own measurements of feature-embedding generalization gaps and classification outcomes after embedding-space oversampling. These findings do not measure the specific behaviors or properties named in V1–V8. The study cites prior work on memorization and generalization; those cited results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study measures feature-range differences and evaluates oversampling for imbalanced classification. These results test none of V1–V8. Memorization/generalization coexistence is cited background; a feature-range gap does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or any other named version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors report larger feature-range gaps for minority classes, an association with classification errors, and improved classification through EOS. Their explanation that expanding embedding ranges improves performance is a hypothesis. The reported gap reduction compares augmented training embeddings with test embeddings; classifier-only retraining leaves the feature extractor fixed.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains CNNs on imbalanced natural image data and measures a class-wise feature-range gap, then evaluates embedding-space oversampling. It does not test arbitrary-label memorization or the optimizer, batch-size, dropout, or sharpness comparisons in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and loss function affect the reported gap patterns; the authors say EOS has less impact on CelebA.

fits_no_version.finding: Feature-range gaps generally increase with class imbalance and are 2 to almost 4 times larger for incorrectly classified test instances than correctly classified instances.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In imbalanced image classification, training-to-test feature-range mismatch is associated with minority-class underrepresentation and classification errors.

fits_no_version.finding: Under cross-entropy, EOS raises balanced accuracy from .7256 to .7581 on CIFAR-10, .8811 to .9016 on SVHN, .5694 to .5794 on CIFAR-100, and .7598 to .8044 on CelebA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EOS augmentation in embedding space followed by classifier retraining can improve balanced accuracy on imbalanced image datasets.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Data Engineering
record.problems: The feature-gap figures do not give numerical values in the text. The study uses imbalanced image datasets and does not test random labels, standard training on natural balanced labels, or most claim-version interventions. Training-set cuts varied by less than 2 balanced-accuracy points, but the reported experiments select a single cut.
record.rows_left_out: Many Table II and Table III balanced-accuracy, geometric-mean, and F1 entries compare additional loss functions and resampling methods. They are not included because the main extracted numeric outcome is the baseline-versus-EOS balanced-accuracy comparison under cross-entropy; the tables are flattened in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Paired random-label fitting and natural-label held-out performance under the same architecture and training recipe.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error and their test-error trajectories.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, accuracy generalization gaps, and ranking against norm or margin measures.
Memorization-based example removal versus equally sized random removal followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels are warranted. Comparisons among CNN architectures in Table V do not test widening beyond interpolation or convolutional versus fully connected generalization. Longer classifier retraining in Figure 7 does not test batch-size effects. States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, not denials of the study's reported findings.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test accuracy.
Network-width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
